contributions: Provides a unified treatment of GNN architectures designed around expressiveness theory, from those achieving the 1-WL upper bound (GIN) to those surpassing it (ID-GNN, k-GNN, subgraph GNNs)
Demonstrates practical implementation details and engineering choices for each architecture, including when simplifications like SGC suffice
Connects theoretical WL hierarchy to concrete architectural designs with empirical validation on benchmarks
limitations: SGC suffers from over-smoothing for large K and fails on heterophilic graphs and graph classification tasks. Higher-order k-GNNs have exponential memory cost O(n^k) and computation O(n^{k+1}), limiting them to small molecular graphs (10–50 nodes). ID-GNN and subgraph GNNs incur O(|V|) multiplicative overhead, making them infeasible for large graphs (100K+ nodes). Subgraph GNNs are predominantly limited to molecular property prediction and small graph classification. The chapter notes that many real benchmarks do not require distinguishing beyond 1-WL, questioning the practical necessity of higher-order architectures.
methods: The chapter surveys and analyzes multiple GNN architectures: GIN uses sum aggregation with an MLP and learnable epsilon to achieve the 1-WL bound; SGC removes all non-linearities between layers, collapsing to a single linear propagation matrix A^K X W; APPNP decouples feature transformation (via MLP) from graph propagation (via personalized PageRank diffusion with teleportation parameter alpha); PNA combines four aggregators (mean, max, min, standard deviation) with three degree scalers (identity, amplification, attenuation) into 12 concatenated features per node; ID-GNN injects target-node identity into message passing to break symmetry; k-GNNs operate on k-tuples of nodes with delta-sparsification; subgraph GNNs run GNNs on ego subgraphs per node; PairNorm enforces minimum pairwise distance between embeddings to counter over-smoothing.
results: SGC achieves accuracy within 1–2% of GCN on Cora, CiteSeer, and PubMed despite being linear. APPNP with alpha=0.1 and K=10 propagation steps outperforms GCN on Cora, CiteSeer, and ogbn-arxiv. On ZINC molecular regression, 3-WL delta-k-GNN reaches MAE below 0.09 compared to 0.16 for GIN, a 44% error reduction. PNA consistently outperforms GIN and GCN on ZINC and OGB molecular benchmarks. PairNorm enables deeper GIN networks without over-smoothing.
tldr: This chapter designs GNN encoders that achieve or provably exceed the 1-WL expressiveness bound, covering GIN (which matches the 1-WL ceiling), SGC, APPNP, PNA, ID-GNN, higher-order k-WL GNNs, subgraph GNNs (ESAN/DS-GNN), and PairNorm as principled responses to specific theoretical limitations.
